Of Johannes Trithemius

...a remarkable change and the new founding of many cities, so that Paris, Mainz, Carthage, Naples, and others arose anew, and kingdoms arose anew, such as those of the Lacedaemonians, Corinthians, Hebrews, and many others. In these times there were very great wars and battles of kings and peoples throughout the whole world, and various changes of empires. From this time the Venetians reckon the beginning both of their people and of their city from the Trojans. And it should be noted that very many other nations, both in Europe and in Asia, claim that they took their origin from the Trojans; to them I have thought fit to grant only as much credence as they themselves can persuade me of the truth by sufficient testimony. Trifling are the things they bring forward about their nobility and antiquity, wishing openly to boast, as though there had been no peoples in Europe before the destruction of the Trojans, and as though there had been no one of ignoble birth among the Trojans themselves. Likewise, under the rule of this planet Saul was made the first king of the Jews; afterward David, whose son King Solomon built at Jerusalem the temple of the true God, most famous in all the world. Hence the Spirit of God, illuminating his prophets with a fuller light of his grace, caused them to foretell not only the future incarnation of the Lord Savior but also many other things, as the sacred histories testify. Among them were Nathan, prophet of King David, Gad, Asaph, Ahijah, Shemaiah, Azariah, Anan, with many others. Homer, the Greek poet and writer of the destruction of Troy, Dares the Phrygian, and Dictys of Crete, who were present at that destruction itself and likewise described it, are read to have been alive in these times.

XIII.

In the thirteenth order, Gabriel, the spirit of the Moon, again took up the government of the world on the thirtieth day of January, in the year from the origin of the universe 4252, and continued in his rule for 354 years and 4 months, until the year of the world 4606 and the fourth month. In this time, moreover, several prophets flourished among the Hebrews, namely Elijah, Elisha, Micah, Obadiah, and very many others. There were also various changes in the kingdom of the Hebrews. Lycurgus gave statutes and laws to the Lacedaemonians. Capetus Silvius, Liberius Silvius, Procas Silvius, and Numitor, kings of Italy, flourished under the guidance of this spirit. Many new kingdoms also took their beginnings under him, such as those of the Lydians, Medes, Macedonians, Spartans, and others. The monarchy of the Assyrians came to an end in Sardanapalus. Likewise the kingdom of the Macedonians was consumed. Various laws were imposed on human beings, and the worship of the true God was neglected; the religion of false gods was propagated exceedingly. The city of Rome was built under the rule of this spirit in the year 1484, which was the 239th year of the government of this Gabriel in order; and the kingdom of the Silvii of Italy failed, and that of the Romans began. In these times also Thales, Solon, Chilon, Periander, Cleobulus, Bias, and Pittacus, the seven sages, flourished in Greece, and from this time philosophers and poets began to be held in esteem. First to rule at Rome was Romulus, founder of the city, for 37 years, a fratricide and cultivator of sedition. After him Numa Pompilius ruled for 42 years; he enlarged the worship of the gods, and in the time of Hezekiah king of the Jews he maintained the kingdom in great peace. Toward the end of the governance of this spirit of the Moon, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, took Jerusalem, destroyed King Zedekiah, and led away the whole people captive. Jeremiah the prophet flourished; he foretold this destruction, and likewise the future liberation from Babylon.

XIV.

After Gabriel, Michael, the spirit of the Sun, again assumed the fourteenth rule of the world. He began on the first day of the month of May, in the year of the world 4606, in the fourth month, and ruled the world in his order for 354 years, until the year from the foundation of the world 4960 and 8 months. In the time of this governance Evil-merodach, king of Babylon, restored liberty and a king to the people of the Hebrews, at the direction of Michael, who, as Daniel writes, stood for the people of the Jews, to whom they had been entrusted by God. Likewise in these times the monarchy of the Persian kingdom began. Its first king was Darius, and its second Cyrus; in the days of Belshazzar they utterly destroyed that most powerful kingdom of Babylon, as Daniel and the prophets had foretold. In these times the Cumaean Sibyl flourished; she offered nine books to King Tarquinius Priscus to be bought at a price. In them were contained the sequence of future warnings and the plan of the whole commonwealth of the Romans. But when the king refused the price, the Sibyl burned the first three books in his sight, and for the remaining six she demanded the same price. When he again refused it, she also handed over another three to the fire to be burned; and she would have done the same with the last ones, had not the king, persuaded by the counsel of his men, redeemed them from destruction by paying the price that had been demanded for all. Likewise, after abolishing kings, the Romans appointed two consuls for each year. Phalaris the tyrant occupied Sicily in those times. Magic too, in those times, was held in great esteem among the kings of the Persians. Pythagoras the philosopher and many others then flourished among the Greeks. The temple at Jerusalem and the city were rebuilt. Ezra the prophet [unclear] the burned books of Moses...

Of Johannes Trithemius

from the Chaldaeans, who were also called Babylonians, restored the use of memory as an archetype. Xerxes, king of the Persians, led an army against the Greeks, but accomplished little. Rome was captured, burned, and destroyed by the Gauls, except only the Capitol, protected by a goose, which roused the weary fighters. The very famous wars of the Athenians also occurred in those times. The philosophers Socrates and Plato lived at that time. The Romans, again abolishing the consuls, established tribunes and aediles, and in these times were involved in many disasters. Alexander the Great also, after the rule of Michael had been completed, reigned in Macedonia. He destroyed the monarchy of the Persians in Darius; by his rule he subjected all Asia, together with part of Europe. He lived twelve years and five months; after his death countless wars followed, and many evils; the monarchy was divided into four. Among the Hebrews a contest began over the high priesthood. The kingdom of Syria begins.

XV.

After Michael, fifteenth in order, now for the third time Orifiel, the spirit of Saturn, assumed the rule of the world on the last day of the month of September, in the year 4960, month 8, from the creation of the universe. He presided for 354 years and 4 months, until the year of the world 5315. Under his rule the Punic War began between the Romans and the Carthaginians. The city of Rome was almost wholly consumed by fire and water. The Colossus, a cast bronze image 126 feet high, fell in an earthquake. In this one year there was peace for the Romans after the Punic War; for 440 years they had never been without war. Jerusalem, together with the temple, was burned and destroyed by Antiochus Epiphanes. The history and wars of the Maccabees were carried on. In these times, in the year 606 from the founding of the city, Carthage was destroyed; it burned for 17 continuous days. In Sicily there was a conspiracy of 7,000 slaves against their masters. Great portents were seen in Europe in those times: domestic animals fled to the woods; blood flowed; a fiery globe flashed from heaven with a crash. Mithridates, king of Pontus and Armenia, waged war with the Romans for 40 years. The kingdom of the Hebrews was restored, which had been interrupted for 575 years, from the time of Zedekiah down to Aristobulus. Likewise the German Teutons invaded the Romans; after many battles they are said to have been defeated, and 160,000 were killed, besides innumerable others who killed themselves together with their households, under the consuls Gaius and Manlius. Nevertheless, many of the Romans had previously been destroyed by them. Finally, the civil wars, which lasted 40 years, greatly wore down the Romans. Three suns appeared at Rome, but not for long, and soon they were reduced to one. A few years later Julius Gaius Caesar usurped the empire of the Romans; Octavian Augustus after him enlarged it, and united Asia, Africa, and Europe into one monarchy. He ruled for 36 years; through him God bestowed peace on the whole world. In the year 751 from the founding of the city, the 42nd of Octavian Caesar Augustus, in the 245th year and 8th month of the aforesaid rule of Orifiel, spirit of Saturn, on the twenty-fifth day of the month of December, JESUS CHRIST, Son of God, was born of the Virgin Mary in Bethlehem of Judaea. Note how beautiful was the ordering of divine providence. For the world was first created under the rule of Orifiel, and under his third rule also was mercifully redeemed, restored, and renewed, so that so great a harmony of events seems to furnish no small credibility to this description of the rule of the world by the seven spirits. For under the first rule of Orifiel there was one monarchy of the whole world; under the second, as we said above, it was divided among many; again under the third, as is seen, it was recalled into unity. It is clear, if we measure rightly, that it is also manifest that under the second rule of Orifiel there was one monarchy of the whole world, when the tower of Babylon was being built. From this time the kingdom of the Jews was taken away, and the victims and continual sacrifice ceased; nor will liberty be restored to the Jews before the third revolution of Michael the spirit; and this will happen after the birth of Christ in the year 1880, month 8, that is, in the year of the world 7170. Sixteenth in order after Orifiel, Anael, the spirit of Venus, [assumed] the rule of the whole world for the third time.

Cessauit tandem persecutio infidelium aduersus Ecclesiam, posteaquam Constantinus Caesar Magnus fidem assumpsit, anno mundi 5539.post medium regiminis ipsius Anae- lis Angeli Veneris, quamuis etiam postea in parte fuerit aliquoties per impios turbata, manfit tamen multo tempore quietissima. Ex hinc genus humanum,quod à tem- pore Nini Regis circa idolorum culturas per annos 2300.miferabiliter errauerat,ad vni- us Dei fuit cognitionem misericorditer reuocatum. Artes variae subtilitatis his tempo- ribus auctae sunt,&amp; per conuenientia naturae ornatum sumpserunt et amp; incremen- tum. Mutantur enim hominum cum tempore mores, &amp; corpora inferiora secundum influentiam superiorum disponuntur. Mens quidem libera est,&amp; influentiam astrorum non sucscipit, nisi prae nimium,quod cùm corpore habet, commercium se inclinando af- fectum commaculet suum. Angeli enim, qui motores sunt Orbium,nihil eorũ qua na- tura constituit, destruunt vel subuertunt. Cometa insolitae magnitudinis Constantini mortem praecessit. Arriana haeresis multis in locis turbauit Ecclesiam sanctam in fine hu- ius regiminis, tempore Iuliani Caesaris cruces apparuerunt,in lineis vestibus hominum. In Asia et amp; Palestina secuta sunt bella, pestilentiae et amp; fames in istis locis in quibus cruces apparuerunt.His quoq: temporibus circa annos Domini 360.Franci in Germania sun- pferunt initium,qui postea Galliam deuastantes suo nomine victam Franciam nuncu- paure. Descriptio Franciae fuit magnitudine longa et amp; lata,cuius Metropolis Moguntia, nunc vero Herbipolis sola.Bauati,Sueui,Rhenenses,Saxones,Thuringi,&amp; circumsi- ti Pontificatus,magnam hodie partem Franciae in Germania occupant.Item anno gu- bernationis huius Anaelis 280.Romanum inclinati coepit imperium,cum vrbs capta fuit à Gottis et amp; incensa,sede prius imperiali sub Constantino in Graeciam translata,quod in- itium fuit et amp; causa rotius inclinationis Monarchiae.Nam circa finem huius regimenti A- naelis surrexerunt Radagifus, Alaricus,Athaulfusque Reges Gottorum.Item postea Gensericus Vandalorum, Athila quoque Hunorum, qui totam Europam peruagantes, imperium miserabiliter lacerauerunt,vt in historiis patet. XVII. POST Anaelem ordine 17. Zachariel spiritus Iouis regimen vniuersale tertia vice resumpsit prima die Ianii,anno mundi 5669.mense 4.Dominicae vero Natiuitatis 463. mense 7.&amp; praefuit annis 354 mensibus quatuor,vsq: ad annos mundi 6023.mensemque 8.Domini autem 8·7.Multi his temporibus amore philosophiae Christianae,fese ad Ere- mum contulerunt,multa etiam apparuere portenta, Cometes, terraemotus,pluuia san- guinis.Merlinus in Tumbae natus miranda praedixit in principio huius regiminis.Arctu- rus (quem vulgo Artum appellant) Rex Britanniae famosissimus barbaros vicit,pacem Ecclesię reddidit, multa praelia victor gessit,fidem Christi ampliauit,Galliam totam, Noruegiam,Daciam et amp; multas prouincias suo imperio subiugauit.Erat omnium sui temporis Regum gloriosissimus, qui post multa egregia patrata, nusquam compa- ruit, multis annis expectatis à Britonibus redire, de quo mirabiles olim Mimi canti- lenas ediderint,quo regnante,Anglia inflore fuit,cui terdena regna feruerunt.Hif- ce temporibus monachorum in Ecclesia Dei ordines coeperunt multiplicari.Theo- doricus Rex Gothorum Arrianus totam Italiam possedit, Boetium consulem occi- dit. Erant omnia perturbatione plena,imperium simul et amp; Ecclesia.Zenon et amp; Anasta- sius Imperatores Arriani in Oriente, Theodoricus et amp; sui successores in Italia,Honorius Rex Vandalorum in Africa tyrannidem exercebant non paruam.Clodoueus tandem Rex Francorum in Gallia factus Christianus et amp; Gothos superauit et amp; pacem rebus impo- fuit, licet non vbique terrarum tempore Sanct.Benedicti, anno Christianorum quingen- tesimo, vel circa in principio regiminis huius Angeli Zacharielis Iouis, cuius est pro- prium spiritus,imperia mutare et amp; regna,quod in hac revolutione factum,multipliciter historiae declarãt,&amp; quod ipse facere nõ potuit Raphaeli Angelo Mercurii sucessori suo faci-

JOHANNES TRITHEMIUS

... resumed it for the second time, on the last day of January, in the year of the creation of heaven and earth 5315, but from the birth of Christ 169; and he governed the world for 354 years and 4 months, up to the year of the world 5669, 4 months, but of the Lord’s Nativity in the flesh 463. And it should be noted that through almost the whole period of this rule of Anael, angel of Venus, the Church of the Christians flourished and prevailed amid persecutions, countless thousands of men being killed for the faith of Christ. Finally, many heresies in these times began to spring up in the Church, which in time were extinguished not without the labor and blood of good men. In these times there flourished many men most learned and eloquent in every kind of knowledge: theologians, astronomers, physicians, orators, historiographers, and others like them, not only among the nations but also among Christians. At length the persecution of unbelievers against the Church ceased after Constantine Caesar the Great accepted the faith, in the year of the world 5539, after the middle of the rule of this Anael, angel of Venus; although even afterwards it was sometimes disturbed in part by impious men, nevertheless it remained very quiet for a long time. From this time the human race, which from the time of King Ninus had wandered wretchedly in the worship of idols for 2300 years, was mercifully called back to the knowledge of one God. Various arts of subtlety were increased in these times, and through the harmonies of nature received adornment and growth. For the morals of men change with time, and lower bodies are disposed according to the influence of the higher ones. The mind indeed is free, and does not receive the influence of the stars, unless, by reason of the too great commerce which it has with the body, it stains its own affection by inclining itself. For the angels, who are the movers of the spheres, destroy or overturn nothing of those things which nature has established.

A comet of unusual magnitude preceded the death of Constantine. The Arian heresy troubled the holy Church in many places at the end of this rule. In the time of Julian Caesar, crosses appeared on men’s linen garments. In Asia and Palestine there followed wars, plagues, and famines in those places in which the crosses had appeared. In these times also, around the year of the Lord 360, the Franks took their beginning in Germany; afterwards, devastating Gaul, they called the conquered land Francia by their own name. The extent of Francia was long and broad in size; its metropolis was Mainz, but now only Würzburg. The Bavarians, Swabians, Rhinelanders, Saxons, Thuringians, and the surrounding bishoprics today occupy a great part of Francia in Germany. Likewise, in the 280th year of the governance of this Anael, the Roman empire began to decline, when the city was captured by the Goths and burned, the imperial seat having previously been transferred under Constantine to Greece; this was the beginning and cause of the decline of the whole monarchy. For around the end of this rule of Anael there arose Radagaisus, Alaric, and Athaulf, kings of the Goths; likewise afterwards Genseric of the Vandals, and also Attila of the Huns, who, roaming through all Europe, wretchedly tore the empire apart, as is clear in the histories.

XVII.

After Anael, in the seventeenth order, Zachariel, spirit of Jupiter, resumed the universal rule for the third time on the first day of January, in the year of the world 5669, the fourth month, but of the Lord’s Nativity 463, the seventh month; and he presided for 354 years and four months, up to the year of the world 6023 and the eighth month, but of the Lord [unclear]. In these times many, through love of Christian philosophy, betook themselves to the desert; many portents also appeared: comets, earthquakes, rain of blood. Merlin, born in Tumba, foretold marvelous things at the beginning of this rule. Arturus, whom the common people call Arthur, the most famous king of Britain, defeated the barbarians, restored peace to the Church, fought many battles as victor, enlarged the faith of Christ, and subjected all Gaul, Norway, Dacia, and many provinces to his rule. He was the most glorious of all the kings of his time; after accomplishing many outstanding deeds, he appeared nowhere, though the Britons expected for many years that he would return. Of him the mimes once produced marvelous songs. In his reign England was in flower, and thirty kingdoms served him. In these times the orders of monks in the Church of God began to multiply. Theodoric, king of the Goths, an Arian, possessed all Italy and killed the consul Boethius. Everything was full of disturbance, both the empire and the Church. Zeno and Anastasius, Arian emperors in the East, Theodoric and his successors in Italy, and Honorius, king of the Vandals, in Africa, exercised no small tyranny. At length Clovis, king of the Franks in Gaul, having become a Christian, both overcame the Goths and imposed peace on affairs, though not everywhere on earth, in the time of Saint Benedict, in the five-hundredth year of the Christians, or thereabouts, at the beginning of the rule of this angel Zachariel of Jupiter, whose proper function as a spirit is to change empires and kingdoms; that this was done in this revolution the histories declare in many ways. And what he himself could not do, he [left] for Raphael, angel of Mercury, his successor, to do...

CHRONOLOGIA MYSTICA. faciendum in Carolo Francorum ordinavit. Multa enim regna sub his 350. annis de- fecerunt, Gothorum, Vandalarum, Burgundiorum, Longobardonorum, Thuringo- norum, Alemanorum, Bauarorum, & alia complura. Iustinianus Imperator primus Rempub. legibus ornavit pulcherrime. Viri sub Zachariae clarissimi plures flore- runt, Iustinianus templum Sanct. Sophiae 400. turrim Constantinopoli extruxit. Impe- rium bipertitum, confusum, & turbationibus plenum crebrius fuit. Signa multa his appa- ruere temporibus, vt est reperiae in historiis. Coṣdrai Perfarum Rex Hierusalem cepit, quem Eracleus poeta occidit, Machomet Arabis Saracenorum sectam introducit hice temporibus circa Christi annum 600. per quam imperium Romanum in Asia ex toro iam cernitur ablatum. Dagobertus Rex Franciae Anglos, qui tune Saxones dicebantur, supe- rans interfecit. Notandum quod fides Christiana paulatim ab hinc in Asia et Africa coe- pit deficere subintrante secta Saracenorum, qua iam totum pene mundum foedavit. Cir- ca annos Domini 774. cruces apparuerunt in vestibus hominum, & non diu postea divifum est imperium Romanorum, facta translatione Monarchiae ad Francos in Caro- lum, qui eripuit de interitu Ecclesiae et imperiae, & geflit praelia multa. Nomen sub eo Westgallorum in Saxonia post victoriam coepit. XVIII. O c t a v o decimo loco post Zachariaelem Iouis Angelum, Raphael spiritus Mer- curii mundi gubernationem tertio fufcepit, 2. die mensis Novembris, anno conditionis vniverfi 6023. menfe 8. Dominica vero natiuitatis 817. & praefuit orbi 454. mensibus 4. vq̄ ad annos mundi 6378. Dominica vero 1171. In principio huius reuolutionis Mo- narchia Romani imperii, ficut diximus, in Carolum Magnu translata eft. Poṣ Carolum filius eius Ludouicus imperavit annis 25. Quo mortuo, filii eius interfe dimicantes, Impe- rii vires rursus extenuarunt. Normanni Galliam deuaftarunt. Roma bis foedatur a Sar- acenis. Sub Ludouico fecundo fanguis pluit e Coelo in Italia per triduum. In Saxonia villa quaedam cum omnibus aedificiis et hominibus in momento abforbeitur hiatu terrae hor- ribili. Circa Domini annos 910. motus in Italia facti funt magni, defecitque Italia ab imperio Francorum, propriosque fibi confiftit Reges, quorum primus fuit Berengarius Dux Föroliuui, cui septem per ordinem fucceflerunt, annis ferme quinquaginta, viq̄ ab imperi- rii translationem in Germanos. Facetusque fuit primus Imperator Otto, & ex hinc Monar- chia reformari coepit, cui filius Otto, & nepos Otto in imperio fucceflerunt, fub quibus couertuntur Hungari ad Christianorum fidem. Otto autem tertius fine liberis mortuus, Electores imperii poṣ fe inftituit, anno Christianorũ 1002. ficuti permanent vq̄ in pra- fentem diē. Hierufalem vero capturà Saracenis. Portenta multa funt vifa in caelo, aere, terra, mari et aquis. Ottone vero tertio mortuo, Henricus primus principum electione fucceflit, imperavit annis 20. qui Bambergensẽm Ecclesiae fundavit et moriens virgo v. na cum vxore Kunigunda miraculis corufcauit: poṣ quem Conradas eligitur primus Dux Francorum, & imperavit annis 20. Item Gorfridus Comes de Bulion terra fanetam, & Hierufalem de manibus infidelium recuperavit. Ante finem reuolutionis multa figna et portenta vifa funt, & paruo elapfo tempore gens Tarrarorum egressa de finibus suis, multa imperio Romano fecit mala, fames, peftilentie et terra motus imperio fuerunt. So- les tres in Oriente vifi funt totidemque Luna, anno Domini 1153. Fridericus I. Barbarossa dictus imperare coepit, & imperavit annis 33. Cuius imperii fuit initium anno Raphae- lis 336. Multa gefsit magnifice, viresque imperii dilatauit, & multa bella feliciter geflit, cu- ius tempore nono Egiani et Lituotrii ad fidem Chrifti conuerfi funt. XIX. N o n o decimo ordine imperium mundi vniverfale fumpfit tertia vice Samael Spi- ritus Martis, tertio die Martii, anno mundi 6378. & gubernavit annis 354. mensibus 4. vq̄ ad annos mundi 6732. menfe 4. Domini vero 1525. Sub cuius regimine multa in orbe terrarum bella fuerunt, quibus infinita hominum millia perierunt, & regna quam plura priftinos terminos amiferunt. Inter Fridericum Imperatorem primum, & Romanos proceres discordia multae fuerunt et praelia magna, & Romanorum multa millia perie- runt. Diaetus Fridericus Mediolanum funditus fubuertit. Leodium deftruitur. Hierufa- lem à Saracenis iterum capturà. Imperium Tarrarorum omnium hoc tempore in orbe maximum his temporibus initium fumpfit, feceruntque in mundo plagam maximam, nec ceffant. Poṣ Fridericum Henricus filius eius ad Imperatorem eligitur. Quo mortuo, fchi- fma confundit imperium fub Philippo et Ottone, & fecuta funt infinib. Germanie praelia multa, Argentine, Colonia, Leodi, Wormatae, Spira, & in toto regno. Mendicantium fecta

Mystical Chronology.

...he ordained that it should be done in Charles of the Franks. For many kingdoms failed in these 350 years: those of the Goths, Vandals, Burgundians, Thuringians, Alemanni, Bavarians, and very many others. The emperor Justinian was the first to adorn the commonwealth most splendidly with laws. Under Zachariel several very famous men flourished; Justinian built the church of Saint Sophia [unclear] a tower at Constantinople. The empire was more often divided in two, confused, and full of disturbances. Many signs appeared in these times, as may be found in the histories. Chosroes, king of the Persians, took Jerusalem; Heraclius later killed him. Muhammad the Arab introduced the sect of the Saracens in these times, around the year of Christ 600; through it the Roman empire in Asia is now seen to have been wholly taken away. Dagobert, king of France, overcame and killed the Angles, who were then called Saxons. It should be noted that from this point the Christian faith gradually began to fail in Asia and Africa, as the sect of the Saracens entered in; it has now defiled almost the whole world. Around the year of the Lord 774, crosses appeared on people’s clothing, and not long afterward the Roman empire was divided, the monarchy being transferred to the Franks in Charles, who rescued the Church and the empire from destruction and fought many battles. Under him, after the victory, the name of the [Westphalians?] in Saxony began.

XVIII.

In the eighth place after Zachariel, the angel of Jupiter, Raphael, the spirit of Mercury, took up the government of the world for the third time, on the second day of the month of November, in the year from the creation of the universe 6023, in the eighth month, but in the year of the Lord’s nativity 817; and he presided over the world for [354?] years and 4 months, until the year of the world 6378, but of the Lord 1171. At the beginning of this revolution, as we have said, the monarchy of the Roman empire was transferred to Charlemagne. After Charles, his son Louis ruled for 25 years. When he had died, his sons, fighting among themselves, again weakened the forces of the empire. The Normans devastated Gaul [unclear] Saracens. Under Louis the Second, blood rained from heaven in Italy for three days. In Saxony a certain village, with all its buildings and people, was swallowed up in a moment by a horrible opening of the earth. Around the years of the Lord 910, great disturbances occurred in Italy, and Italy broke away from the empire of the Franks and set up kings of its own; the first of them was Berengar, duke of Friuli, and seven succeeded him in order, for almost fifty years, down to the transfer of the empire to the Germans. Otto became the first emperor, and from this point the monarchy began to be restored; his son Otto and his grandson Otto succeeded him in the empire. Under them the Hungarians were converted to the Christian faith. Otto the Third, dying without children, established the electors of the empire after him, in the year of the Christians 1002, as they remain to the present day. Jerusalem, however, was taken by the Saracens. Many portents were seen in heaven, air, earth, sea, and waters. When Otto the Third had died, Henry was the first to succeed by election of the princes; he ruled for 20 years. He founded the Church of Bamberg, and, dying a virgin together with his wife Kunigunda, shone with miracles. After him Conrad was elected, the first duke of the Franks, and he ruled for 20 years. Likewise Godfrey, count of Bouillon, recovered the Holy Land and Jerusalem from the hands of the infidels. Before the end of the revolution many signs and portents were seen, and after a short time had elapsed the people of the Tartars, going forth from their own borders, did many evils to the Roman empire. Famines, pestilences, and earthquakes occurred in the empire. Three suns were seen in the East, and the same number of moons, in the year of the Lord 1153. Frederick I, called Barbarossa, began to rule, and he ruled for 33 years. The beginning of his rule was in the 336th year of Raphael. He performed many deeds magnificently, enlarged the forces of the empire, and successfully waged many wars; in his time [unclear] and [unclear] were converted to the faith of Christ.

XIX.

In the nineteenth order Samael, the spirit of Mars, took up the universal empire of the world for the third time, on the third day of March, in the year of the world [6378?], and governed for 354 years and 4 months, until the year of the world 6732, in the fourth month, but of the Lord 1525. Under his rule there were many wars throughout the world; in them countless thousands of people perished, and very many kingdoms lost their former boundaries. Between Frederick the First, emperor, and the Roman nobles there were many discords and great battles, and many thousands of Romans perished. The said Frederick overthrew Milan from its foundations. Jerusalem was again taken by the Saracens. The empire of all the Tartars, the greatest in the world at this time, took its beginning in these times; they inflicted a very great scourge on the world, and they do not cease. After Frederick, his son Henry was chosen emperor. When he had died, schism threw the empire into confusion under Philip and Otto, and many endless battles followed in Germany, at Strasbourg, Cologne, Liege, Worms, Speyer, and throughout the whole kingdom. The sect of the mendicants

Destruction of many kingdoms. Justinian the emperor. Church of Saint Sophia. Chosroes. Muhammad. Dagobert. Noteworthy. Charles the emperor. Transfer of the Roman empire to the Franks. Rain of blood. Chasm in Saxony. Transfer of the Roman empire to the Germans; [unclear]. Conversion of the Hungarians to the faith of Christ. Origin of the prince-electors. Henry I, founder of the Church of Bamberg. Three suns in the East. Destruction of Milan. Incursions of the Tartars. Rumors of wars. Decline of the faith.

JOHANNIS TRITEMIL lecta his temporibus instituitur, anno Samaelis 40. vel circa. Vnde certum est omnia providentia fieri. Sarraceni multa praelia adversus Christianos in Asia et Africa gesserunt. Constantinopolis capitur a Germanis, & Balduinus Flandriae Comes Imperator instituitur. Ex Alemania pueri plus quam 20000. a pyratis merguntur in mari, qui vano spiritu seduerti se terram sanctam recuperatos dicebant. Ex Hispania coadunati paftores pecorum muli Parilius accedentes, bona clericorum rapuerunt, populo congratu- lante. Sed cum manus in Laicorum extenderunt bona, necati sunt. Anno Christianorum 1212. Fridericus secundus eligitur, imperavit annis 33. qui multa contra Ecclesiae egit. Anno 1238. Eclipsis et terra motus continui multa hominum millia oppraerentur. Frisia quoque per maritimos fluetus pene tota submerita fuit et perierunt plus quam 100000. homínium. Tartari Hungariam deuastant atq Poloniaem. Armenia maiori prius, & multis su- peratis regionibus. Anno Christianorum 1244. quidam Iudaeus apud Toletum fodiens, librum inuenit, in quo erat scriptum: In tertio mundo Christus nascetur de Virgine Maria, & pro salute hominum patietur. mox credens baptizatus est. Tertius mundus, tertia Saturni spiritus reuolutio fuit, de qua supra dictum est, in cuius principio Christus fuit de Virgine natus. Romani Pontifices Fridericum abrogantes imperio 28. annis vacasse di- xerunt, vtq ad electionem Rodolphi Comitis de Habspurgo, inter reges constituentes, Principum electione, primo Henricum Comitem de Schwartzenburg Thuringum, Wilhelmum Comitem Holandia, Conradum filium Friderici, Alphonsum Regem Ca- stella, & Richardum Comitem Cornubia fraterem Regis Angliae, & multiplicata sunt mala in terra. Hoc tempore circa annos Domini 1260. Suitensium confoederatio pri- mum coepit gens, parua numero, quae cum tempore creuit et multos nobilium alios in- terfecerunt, alios de finibus fugerunt, viri bellicosi, quorum Respubli. nota est omnibus Germaniae populis. Anno Christianorum 1273. Rudolphus de Habspurgo electione Prin- cipum Imperator constituitur, & imperavit annis 18. vir per omnia prudentis et optimus, de quo Duces Austriae omnes postea descenderunt. Tartari terras Christianorum, Constantinopolim et Greciam inuadentes, multa damna Christianis intulerunt. Sarraceni multas in Asia ciuitates occupant, & plus quam 4. centies Christianorum interficiunt. Rudolpho mortuo, Adolphus de Naflau in Regem electus est, & imperavit annis 6. quae Albertus filius Rudolphi postea superans in bello iuxta Wormatiaem occidit, & Impera- tor electus fuit anno 1298. imperavit 3. annis 10. & à fratri filio interfectur. Ordo Tem- plariorum iussu Clementis Papae quinti destruitur. Insula Rhodus per Christianos de manibus Sarracenorum capta est, anno 4. obfisidion et belli contra eos continui. Alber- to per nepotem occiso, Henricus 8. Imperator constitutus, Comes Lucenburgensis, qui imperavit annis quinque. Quo mortuo Ludovicus quartus Bauariae imperat annis 32. incipiens anno 1315. cui Romani Pontifices coronam dederunt. Fridericus Dux Austriae se opposuit, sed ab eo superatus est. Post Ludovicum Carolus quartus Bohemiae Rex, Imperator constitutur, qui Episcopatum Pragensem in Archiepiscopatum erexit, imperavit annis 31. Terra motus maximi fuerunt. Hic Carolus multa circa Telonea de novo instituit in favorem Principum Electorum. Guntherus Comes de Schwartzaeburg, fe Regem appellatans, Carolo Imperatori opposuit, fed nihil aduersus eum prequaluit. Post Carolum filius eius Wenceslaus imperavit annis 22. post quem Iodocus Marchio Mor- aviae succedit Sigismundo Wenceslai germaniae. Leupoldus dux Austriae cum 8. Comiti- bus et plus 4000. a Suitensibus in bello dimicans occidus est. Sub Wenceslao Bohemo- rum Rege et Imperatore, dogma Hussitarum initium sumpit. Wenceslaus fuit depo- situs: quo depósito, Rupertus Comes Palatinus Rheni Bauariaeque dux fuit electus, & im- peravit annis 10. Anno Domini 1369. Sarracenis bellum induxerunt Christiani, fed ma- le succellit propter arrogantiam Gallorum, quia plus quam 100000. nostrorum occu- buerunt, praeter captivos, inter quos fuit Johannes Burgundiorum Dux, multa fuerunt his temporibus bella. Anno 1407. Sigismundus fit Imperator annis 27. Bohemiae vafta- re conatus est, pro exturbatione haeresium, fed parum profecit. Regum Franciae per Anglos et Burgundiones atrociter vaftatur, affligitur. Sigismundo vita defuncto Albertus dux Austriae, gener eius succedit, anno Christianorum 1438. regnauit 2. annis dumtaxat duobus, vir optimus et imperio dignus. Quo mortuo, Fridericus III. dux Austriae, Ernesti filius, electione Principum Imperator constitutus fuit, & annis 56. imperauit, vir ingenio divinus, & animo pacificus. Anno domini 1440. coepit regnare. Anno Christianorum 1453. Constantinopolis traditione cuiusdam Ianuenfis à Turcis capi- tur, & paulatim tota Graecia defecit à fide Christiana. Johannes Trithemius

A sect was founded in these times, in the year 40 of Samael, or thereabouts. Hence, for the rest, it is that all things happen by providence. The Saracens waged many battles against the Christians in Asia and Africa. Constantinople was taken by the Germans, and Baldwin, Count of Flanders, was made emperor. From Germany more than 26,000 children were drowned at sea by pirates; seduced by a vain spirit, they said that they were going to recover the Holy Land. From Spain, herdsmen gathered together, admitting no one to Paris, seized the goods of the clergy, while the people rejoiced. But when they stretched out their hands to the goods of the laymen, they were killed. In the year of the Christians 1212 Frederick II was elected; he ruled for 33 years, and did much against the Church.

In the year 1238 an eclipse and earthquakes continually crushed many thousands of people. Frisia too was almost submerged by sea-floods, and more than 100,000 people perished. The Tartars devastated Hungary and Poland, after first overcoming Greater Armenia and many regions. In the year of the Christians 1244, a certain Jew at Toledo, while digging, found a book in which it was written: “In the third world Christ will be born of the Virgin Mary and will suffer for the salvation of men.” Believing at once, he was baptized. The third world was the third revolution of the spirit of Saturn, of which mention was made above; at its beginning Christ was born of the Virgin. The Roman pontiffs, removing Frederick from the empire, declared that it had been vacant for 28 years, until the election of Rudolf, Count of Habsburg, whom they set among the kings. By election of the princes, first Henry, Count of Schwarzburg, a Thuringian; William, Count of Holland; [Conrad?], son of Frederick; Alfonso, King of Castile; and Richard, Earl of Cornwall, brother of the King of England; and evils were multiplied on the earth. At this time, around the year of the Lord 1260, the confederation of the Swiss first began: a people small in number, which grew with time and killed many of the nobles, driving others from their borders; warlike men, whose commonwealth is known to all the peoples of Germany. In the year of the Christians 1273 Rudolf of Habsburg was made emperor by election of the princes, and ruled for 18 years, a man in all respects prudent and excellent, from whom all the later dukes of Austria descended. The Tartars, invading the lands of the Christians, Constantinople, and Greece, inflicted much damage on the Christians. The Saracens occupied many cities in Asia and killed more than four hundred thousand Christians. When Rudolf died, Adolf of Nassau was elected king and ruled for 6 years; afterward Albert, son of Rudolf, defeated him in battle near Worms, killed him, and was elected emperor in the year 1298; he ruled for 10 years and was killed by his brother’s son. The order of the Templars was destroyed by Pope Clement V. The island of Rhodes was taken by Christians from the hands of the Saracens in the fourth year of the siege and of continuous war against them. After Albert was killed by his nephew, Henry VIII, Count of Luxembourg, was made emperor, and ruled for five years. When he died, Louis IV of Bavaria ruled for [12?] years, beginning in the year [1315?]; the Roman pontiffs gave him the crown. Frederick, Duke [unclear]. Charles IV, King of Bohemia, emperor. Earthquake. Tolls. [Charles’s?] son Wenceslaus, emperor. [The Duke] of Austria opposed him, but was defeated by him. After Louis, Charles IV, King of Bohemia, was made emperor; he raised the bishopric of Prague to an archbishopric and ruled for 31 years. There were very great earthquakes. This Charles newly instituted many things concerning tolls in favor of the prince-electors. Günther, Count of Schwarzburg, calling himself king, opposed Emperor Charles, but prevailed in nothing against him. After Charles, his son Wenceslaus ruled for [112?] years; after him Jodocus, Margrave of Moravia, succeeded Sigismund, brother of Wenceslaus. Leopold, Duke of Austria, with 8 counts and more than 4,000 men, was killed fighting in battle by the Swiss. Under Wenceslaus, king and emperor of the Bohemians, the teaching of the Hussites took its beginning. Wenceslaus was deposed; after his deposition, Rupert, Count Palatine of the Rhine and Duke of Bavaria, was elected, and ruled for 10 years. In the year of the Lord [1369?], the Christians brought war upon the Saracens, but it went badly because of the arrogance of the French, since they killed more than 100,000 of our men, besides the captives, among whom was John, Duke of the Burgundians. There were many wars in these times. In the year [1407?] Sigismund became emperor for 27 years. He tried to lay waste Bohemia for the extirpation of heresies, but made little progress. The kingdom of France was cruelly laid waste and afflicted by the English and the Burgundians. When Sigismund departed this life, Albert, Duke of Austria, his son-in-law, succeeded him in the year of the Christians 1438; and he ruled for [56?] years, a man divine in intellect and peaceful in spirit. In the year of the Lord 1440 he began to reign. In the year of the Christians 1453 Constantinople was taken by the Turks through the betrayal of a certain Genoese, and gradually all Greece fell away from the Christian faith. For thereafter in time many

Mystical Chronology.

The kingdoms and provinces of the Christians are devastated and captured by the Turks. At this time Christians had many very grave wars among themselves in Gaul, England, Saxony, Westphalia, Prussia, Flanders, Swabia, and other places. In these times the art of printing was newly invented at Mainz, the metropolis of Germany, by wondrous industry, a gift of divinity. In the year of the Christians 1456, the Turks were overthrown in Hungary by the faithful, and many perished. The pilgrimage of children to Saint Michael was remarkable. There were earthquakes in the kingdom of Naples; more than 4,000 men perished. In the year of the Lord 1462, Mainz, the metropolis of the Franks, was captured and plundered. Charles, duke of Burgundy, defeated the French in the year 1465. Afterwards, in the year 67, he destroyed Dinant and Liège. In the year 1473 he entered Guelders and powerfully obtained it, likewise the whole duchy of Lorraine. A comet appeared through the month of January in the year of the Lord 1472. Charles, duke of Burgundy, besieged the town of Neuss for the space of a year, in the year 74; afterwards, in 1477, he was killed in battle, a magnanimous prince.

In these times the Turks took many cities of the Christians: Negroponte in Euboea, also the Bosnian kingdom, the duchy of the [Despot?], Achaia, Mitylene, and several kingdoms in the East. In 1476 a gathering of fools took place at Niklashausen in the Franconia of Germany, full of errors. In the year 1480 the Turks besieged the Rhodians with a great army, but did not prevail. In the same year, departing from Rhodes, they took Hydruntum, more than 12,500 Christians being killed and only 22 escaping by flight. And in the following year the emperor of the Turks, Mehmed, died; Bayezid, his first-born, succeeded him in the kingdom, now ruling into his twenty-seventh year. In the year of the Christians 1486, Maximilian, son of Frederick, was established king of the Romans at Frankfurt; he was greeted as Caesar by Pope Julius in the year 1508. He founded the military order of Saint George against the heretical Turks; he subdued the Swiss in war; he attacks the rebellious Sicambri in war even to this day, and will prosper against all treaty-breakers. The king of the French, persecutor of the Empire in his usual manner, has been found to be devising new plots. May the Almighty protect those assigned to the dominion of Samael in the year [1508?]. The Venetians, rebels against Caesar’s empire, have been marked by ban and war. There will be punishment for obstinacy, and reward for prudent satisfaction.

Around the end of this third revolution of Samael, the image of alteration will pass to the first; it will be the destruction of many. For unless Y., with God ministering, is brought back to Algos, there will be the monarchy of someone, or the transfer of some great kingdom. A great sect of religion will arise, the destruction of old religions. It is to be feared lest the fourth beast lose one head. In Samael, Mars first foretold the Flood, in the second the destruction of Troy; in the third, near the end, there will be great damage to unity. For from preceding things let the future things that follow be judged. This third revolution of Mars will not be completed without the prophecy of some new institution of religion. From here, in the year of the Christians 1508, there remain years up to the year of the world 7086, the eighth month; but of the Lord’s nativity, 1879, likewise two months. The future sequence of this revolution requires prophecy.

I have not written these things assertively, most sacred Caesar; they are by no means to be believed with any injury to the orthodox faith. There are, however, those who have reckoned the months in these matters as lunar; if you decide that they should be agreed with, those things which I have written otherwise must be changed. With my own hand also I protest, and with my mouth I confess, that in all these things I believe nothing, admit nothing, except what the Catholic Church believes; the rest I reject and despise as vain, fabricated, and superstitious.

Praise to almighty God.

Letter of Johannes Trithemius, Abbot of St James, formerly of Spanheim, to the most reverend father in Christ and prince, Lord Laurentius, of the noble and very ancient family of the Bibras, bishop of the distinguished Church of Würzburg and sole duke of Eastern Francia, concerning the compendium of the first volume of the annals on the origin of the Franks.

To the most reverend father in Christ, most excellent prince and lord, Lord Laurentius, bishop of the noble Church of Würzburg and sole duke of Eastern Francia, Johannes Trithemius, unprofitable, and abbot in name alone of the poor little monastery of St James the Apostle in the suburbs of the aforementioned city of Würzburg, offers ready service in all things, no less voluntary than owed by right.

Most reverend father, illustrious prince, and gracious lord, I have written, as your Most Reverend Lordship knows, three great volumes, the work of no small labor, on the origin, course, and particular deeds of the kings, dukes, princes, and people of the Franks, taking the beginning of my narration and of the succession of the kings from the four hundred and fortieth year before the birth of Christ, at which time, after Antenor, the great king of the people, had been killed by enemies, his son Marcomer succeeded to the kingdom and led out his people, namely our forebears, from Scythia, from the borders to the borders of Germany and Saxony, to the mouths of the Rhine, where Guelders now is. In these three volumes I have embraced a period of one thousand nine hundred fifty-four years, in which the kings of the Franks, succeeding one another in proper order, from that same Marcomer already named down to the twentieth year of Maximilian Augustus, emperor of the Romans and Caesar, are counted as one hundred and three. There were many collateral kings, outside the direct line of genealogy, who are excluded from this number of kings. Through the whole first volume, moreover, I continue the successions of the kings of the Franks and their deeds down to King Pippin, exclusively, over one thousand one hundred ninety years, in which there were sixty-one kings succeeding one another in a direct line. Pippin was succeeded by his son Charles, surnamed the Great. After him came his son, Louis the Pious. When he died, his sons divided the kingdom of the Franks into very many parts. When they too had departed this life, their grandsons again the kingdom of the Franco-

Manifestum est enim, quod Franci ab origine semper fuerint

[unclear] in such a manner divided principally into two kingdoms; of these one is to be called, to be, and to remain Germanic, the other Gallic, and neither is to be subject to the other. And this division is such as follows.

The kingdom of the Franks, Germany, is to have perpetually by itself its own king, subject to no mortal whatsoever, not even to the Roman Empire, but, according to the ancient custom of the Franks, most free. To this kingdom, in the aforesaid division, fell the subject nations, cities, peoples, and races: namely the whole kingdom of Germany, with the Saxons, Thuringians, Marcomanni, Danes, Frisians, Hessians, [Westphalians?], East Franks, Bavarians, Swabians, Bohemians, Sorbs, southern Germans, and all the nations, peoples, and races that lie among those named above.

Likewise the whole kingdom of Austrasia, with these cities: Metz, the whole of what is now called Lorraine, Trier, with the Mosellans, the Eifel people, and the [Cinonotes?], Cologne, Aachen, Liege, and both lower and upper Utrecht, with Holland, Zeeland, Brabant, Hainaut, the entire region from the river Rhine westward as far as the sea; with the Tongrians, Flemings, Morini, and the whole land that either adjoins or lies between the aforesaid regions and cities.

Finally, the kingdom of Arles, with its eight counties in Gaul, is considered from ancient times subject to the rule of the king of the Germans. For this reason the archbishop of Trier, whoever he may be at the time, is afterwards known to have been appointed archchancellor of the German kingdom throughout Gaul, for the aforesaid kingdom of Arles. The kingdom of Burgundy also, with all its counties, was assigned in the same division to the kingdom of the Germans. All Alemannia as well, with its cities and peoples, in which are the cities of Chur, Sion, and [Valais?], fell by lot to the kingdom of the Germans, together with the Swiss, Alsatians, [Caurici?], Savoyards, people of Constance, Basel, Strasbourg, Speyer, Worms, Mainz, and all peoples from the rising of the river Rhine as far as the sea, into which it flows by three mouths.

But the Roman Empire, together with Italy, Lombardy, and all those subject to it by ancient right, except Greece, the Eastern Empire, was, and today remains, annexed and subject to the kingdom of the Germans. Nevertheless, over time many disputes, invasions, and changes arose between the kings of the Germans and the Gauls concerning certain boundaries of the kingdom; of these matters it has been written more fully in the second volume.

The kingdom of the Franks of Gaul also, now divided from ours already mentioned, is in like manner, as the constitution declares, to have its own free king, who is no less free than the king of Germany and is subject to no one at all. For it is manifest that the Franks from their origin have always been

fuerint liberrimi, &amp; neque Romanis nec alteri cuiusuis genti vn- quam seruierunt aut extiterunt subiecti, quin potius ipsi Romanorum destruxerunt imperium, sibiꝙ́ fecere subiectum. Et propterea Reges ambo, in diuisione regni pristinam libertatem vbiqꝫ alteri alter illasam seruare statuerunt. had been very free, and never served the Romans nor any other nation whatsoever, nor existed as subjects, but rather they themselves destroyed the empire of the Romans and made it subject to themselves. And for this reason both kings, in the division of the kingdom, determined that each should preserve everywhere the ancient liberty of the other unimpaired.

But the king of Gallic France, in the division of the monarchy, received as his portion the kingdom of Neustria, or Paris, and also the kingdom of Orléans, the kingdom of Aquitaine, the kingdom of [Toulouse?], the kingdom of Armorica, or New Britain, with all the provinces and peoples of inner Gaul, as far as Spain: from the river Rhône as far as the western sea.

After that division of the kingdom of the Franks, I too compressed the history, henceforth leaving aside the Gallic Franks; in the second and third volumes of the Annals I continued the narrative concerning only the German Franks. But since, in so long a course of years, reckoning first from the entrance of the people into Germany, the history became rather lengthy, I judged it worth the effort if from those three volumes of annals I should draw out as many shorter books, which would contain in summary the names, successions, and deeds more worthy of remembrance of the kingdom of the Franks of Germany. For I know that your most reverend Lordship both delights in ancient histories and, by reason of administering your principality, is continually occupied in many affairs. Since, therefore, no prince lives today among mortals to whom, after God, I am by right more bound and more ready, with the most submissive will, to serve and please according to my strength and beyond, than to your most excellent and most reverend Lordship, I judge no one more worthy to whose name I either ought or wish to dedicate these lucubrations of mine concerning the origin of the Franks. Therefore, I pray, may your gracious Lordship kindly receive the work of compendium which I offer, and hold me, your humble servant, commended.

In the year 1515.

A

A Compendium or Abridgment of the First Volume of the Chronicles or Annals of Johannes Trithemius, Abbot of Saint James the Greater, Apostle, in the suburb of the city of Würzburg, concerning the origin of the nation and kings of the Franks, addressed to the most reverend father and prince in Christ, Lord Laurentius, Bishop of Würzburg and Duke of Eastern Francia, begins.

With the aid of our Lord Jesus Christ, we have written, not without very great labors, three volumes of our annals, of by no means small size. In them, from the origin of the nation of the Franks down to the twenty-eighth year of Caesar Maximilian Augustus, we have set forth a fuller history, distinguished in the following order of division. For in the first volume we described both the origin and the kings of the aforesaid nation of the Franks, beginning from Marcomitus, who began to reign in the four hundred thirty-ninth year before the birth of Christ. After the death of his father, whom the Goths had killed in war, he reigned twenty-eight years, and was the first to lead the nation from the mouths of the Danube into Germany, to the mouths of the Rhine. This people, once sprung from Trojan fugitives, while they were still among their own fellow-citizens, had the Trojan name; afterward, scattered among various nations and wandering, they very often changed their name together with their settlements. For at first, when they were called Trojans, they were Trojans; afterward, among the Scythians, they too were named Scythians; but when they came into the borders of Germany, for a time they were called Sicambri; finally, from Francus their king, they were called Franks. Nevertheless the Sicambri could not at once obtain from the neighboring peoples, especially from the Roman Gauls, to whom their power was always suspect, that they should be called Franks, until at last, expanding their kingdom and name, they powerfully subjected to themselves the Romans, together with Italy and all Gaul. And because they lived with the Germans, they were more often named Germans than Franks by the writers of deeds. Thus the whole period of the first volume of our annals contains 1,189 years, from Marcomirus down to King Pippin.

The second volume of the annals takes its beginning from the year of the Lord's nativity 750, when Pippin, mayor of the palace, was elected king of the Franks, Hilderic having been shorn as a monk. From there down to the eighth year of Richard, king of Germany, who succeeded William amid the dissension of the princes, it contains a period of 515 years, as is clear to one who counts the sequence of the order; in these years the history of the German kingdom is woven together.

The third volume of annalistic notes takes its beginning from the eighth year of King Richard, which was the 1266th year of the Lord's nativity. This we have continued to the twenty-eighth year of King Maximilian, namely the 1514th year of the Lord's nativity, containing 248 years. And thus the whole period of the three volumes makes 1,953 years, whose deeds we have embraced.

2 COMPENDIVM LIB. I. Itaque primi voluminis annalium nostrorum epitomen, compendiū siue Brettiarium ex certa mentis nostrae consideratione scripturi, monemus lectorem, ne prius carpat opus, quam prudenter examinet. Temerarii hominis indicium est manifestum, iudicare quod nesciat, & seire neminem posse,quod ipse forsitan ignorat. Scio multos de origine Francorum varie diuersa scripsisse, quorum nonnulli gentem contendunt indigennam,caeteri vero nescio de qua Sic ambrorum vrbe aduentitiam. Quorum diuersas opiniones neminem possse vel discernere vel concordare credimus, quem Hunibaldi compilatione non illustrat. Is etenim solidus Francorum historiographus claruit in humanis Clodocei regis, quem sanctus Remigius praesul Romanorum baptizauit, temporibus, anno dominice nativitatis quingentesimo ; scripsit post Doracum philosophum, Wast-haldum historicum, alios plures rerum gestarum antiquissimos scriptores insigne opus, quod in libros decem octo distinxit.In sex primis, gentis Francorum primaeuam deducit originem ab excidio Troiano vsque ad mortem Antenoris regis, quem Scanziani, Gothi,Suecique siue Suedi,circa Danubij ostia interfecerunt,anno videlicet ante Christi natiuitatem quadringentésimo quadragesimo. In alijs vero sex libris,tempus complectitur ab interitu regis Antenoris memorati,vsque ad Faramundum regem Francorum, secundi ordinis quadragesimum tertium. A Faramundo reliqui sex libri continuantur vssque ad vltimum annum Clodocei primi ex regibus Christiani, qui obiit anno dominicae nativitatis quingentesimo quartodecimo. Et quia de omnibus his in primo volumine annalium nostrorum scripsum,is ratio nominis Breuiarij postulat,vt isticebrenitati studeamus.Finis adest Prooemij. IOANNIS TRITHEMII ABBATIS DIVI IACOBI VVIRCIPVRGENSIS, ORDI- NI SANCTI BENEDICTI, BREVIARVM PRIMI VO- LVMINIS ANNALIVM SVORVM FOELICITER incipit. A NNO siquidem ante natiuitatem domini, saluatoris nostri JesusChristi ex Maria semper intacta virgine quadringentesimo quadragésimo,sedentibus ad Scythiae fines maritimos, haudprocul ab hostijs Danubij,populis,q; postra Franci sunt dicti, antea vero Scythae, sed anterius Troiani,dominabatur Antenor rex, contra quem gens ferocissima, sine numero numerosa,de insulis Scanzianis,quenunc Gothicae nuncupantur,egressa, populum eius crebra incurssione contriuit,arma conferens armis, manibus manus Antenor, nunc victus,nuncelector,postremo fuit à Gothis in bello cum multis suorum occisus,anno praenotato,ante Christi natiuitatem,vt diximus,cCCCXL.cui filius eius Marecomir in regno successit. MARCOMIRVS Antenoris regis perempti maior natu filius, post patrem substitutus,regnauit octo viginti annis:coepitque eodem pene anno, quo pater fuitoccisus.Vir erat magnanimus,fortis,audax, bellicosus,qui necem patris in Gothis viciniores erebris incursionibus vindicavit, quanquam Gothis numero pugnatorum, viribus,longe videretur inferior.Anno praeterea regni sui quarto, cum prioribus regni consilium habuit, quemadmodum aut Gothi arcerentur à regno,aut si hoc fieri nonpossset,alio modo praeuideretur genti,ne periret. Complacuit postremo cunctis,q; recte sapiebant,eo qod tam immensae multitudini Gothorum nequaquam possent resistere,sedes deorum nutu mutare.Conuocatis igitur deorum ministris,quo versum iuberent eundum,à numinibus sciicitarenatur,maiores preceperunt.Parantur officia vaticinijs apta,sacrificia offeruntur infernalib; euocandis arte composita,stat in medio furens ante louis arã facerdos,caput distrorquet.carmina sub marmure profert,dẽtibus arete stridet,curuatis praeter digitis brachiacũ manibus tortuat,vibrat,ac volitans instar recuruat,sano videnti,stulto insano simili-videndus ꝗ homini.Euocatum postremo carmine numẽ,precāti vaticinium Menol-porependit, sic orsus fulminabat: Marcomir Louis princeps,se numen iubet esse tranquillum,nec formidare casus itineris longi,quod tendit in occasum post fratres ad ostia Rheni,quo dorsi am tenesBrutus, Consilium Francorum de transmontane Germania. Responsum Iouis petunt peracerdotes. Iouis vaticinus consilium faceretur templo. Marcomir pꝛeꝑuit in Germania regnus an-nū 28.

Compendium, Book I.

And so, intending from a fixed consideration of our mind to write an epitome of the first volume of our Annals, a compendium or breviary, we warn the reader not to censure the work before he has prudently examined it. It is the manifest mark of a rash man to judge what he does not know, and to think that no one can know what he himself perhaps does not know. I know that many have written various and divergent things about the origin of the Franks: some of them maintain that the people was native-born, while others that it was immigrant from I know not what city of the Sicambri. We believe that no one can either distinguish or reconcile their diverse opinions unless Hunibald’s compilation enlightens him. For that sound historian of the Franks flourished in human life in the times of King Clodoceus, whom Saint Remigius, prelate of the Romans, baptized, in the five-hundredth year of the Lord’s nativity; after Doracus the philosopher, Wasthald the historian, and many other very ancient writers of deeds, he wrote a distinguished work, which he divided into eighteen books. In the first six he traces the earliest origin of the people of the Franks from the Trojan destruction down to the death of King Antenor, whom the Scanzians, Goths, and Sueci or Suedi killed near the mouths of the Danube, namely in the four-hundred-fortieth year before Christ’s nativity. In the other six books he embraces the time from the death of the aforementioned King Antenor down to Faramund, king of the Franks, the forty-third of the second order. From Faramund the remaining six books are continued down to the last year of Clodoceus, the first Christian among the kings, who died in the five-hundred-fourteenth year of the Lord’s nativity. And because I have written about all these things in the first volume of our Annals, the rationale of the name Breviary requires that we here pursue brevity. Here ends the Proem.

The breviary of the first volume of his Annals, by Johannes Trithemius, abbot of Saint James at Würzburg, of the Order of Saint Benedict, happily begins.

Indeed, in the four-hundred-fortieth year before the nativity of the Lord, our Savior Jesus Christ, from Mary ever an untouched virgin, when the peoples who were afterward called Franks, but previously Scythians, and still earlier Trojans, were settled by the maritime borders of Scythia, not far from the mouths of the Danube, King Antenor ruled. Against him a most fierce people, numerous beyond number, having come forth from the Scanzian islands, which are now called Gothic, wore down his people by repeated attack, bringing arms against arms, hands against hands. Antenor, now defeated, now [unclear], was at last killed by the Goths in battle with many of his men, in the year noted above, before Christ’s nativity, as we have said, 440; his son Marcomir succeeded him in the kingdom.

The First King.

Marcomir, the elder son of the slain King Antenor, placed in his father’s stead, reigned twenty-eight years; and he began in almost the same year in which his father was killed. He was a magnanimous, strong, bold, warlike man, who avenged his father’s death upon the nearer Goths by repeated attacks, although he seemed far inferior to the Goths in number of fighters and in strength. Moreover, in the fourth year of his reign he held counsel with the chief men of the kingdom as to how either the Goths might be kept away from the kingdom, or, if this could not be done, provision might be made for the people in some other way, lest it perish.

At last it pleased all who judged rightly that, since they could in no way resist so immense a multitude of Goths, they should change their settlements by the will of the gods. Therefore, after the ministers of the gods had been summoned, the elders commanded that inquiry be made of the divine powers in which direction they ordered them to go. The rites suited to prophecies are prepared; sacrifices are offered by an art composed for summoning infernal powers. In the midst, before the altar of Jove, stands a frenzied priest; he twists his head about, utters songs in a murmur, gnashes tightly with his teeth, with his fingers bent back twists and shakes his arms with his hands, and, darting about, bends backward in like manner, appearing to a sane beholder like a foolish, insane man. At last, after the divine power had been summoned by song, the priest Menolpor, asked for a prophecy, gave response and began to thunder thus: “Marcomir, prince of Jove, the divinity bids itself be tranquil, and not to fear the hazards of the long journey, because he tends westward after his brothers to the mouths of the Rhine, where [unclear] Brutus, [unclear].”

Counsel of the Franks concerning transmontane Germany. They seek the response of Jove through the priests. Jove’s prophet [unclear] that counsel should be made in the temple.

Marcomir ruled in Germany for twenty-eight years.

ANNAL. TRITHEMII. 3 Brutus faciem Troes exul Romphaea quietur. Vierque tibi natura frater est et gente fidelis amicus. Ite preparat as celeri cursu percipite sedes, numine patris tertium dilatandas in orbem. Eadem nocte Marcomirus rex incantatione patria numen vocauit, praecinendo murmure, quam vaticinantem à sagacitate nominauerunt Alirunam, comparauit monstrum, ratificauit auctoritate Sybilli vaticinium sacerdotis, iussit illico traducere gen tem, quo soboles multiplicata nimium praesignante visione maneret fortiorin aeternũ. Numen triceps Marcomir us astare conspexit, vniuscuiusque capitis singulare audi uit prognosticon, diseretumque vidit diadema, vnicuique super eminere impossitum. Primum, caput suit Bufonis: secundum vero, Leonis : tertium, Aquilae in forma qua 10 si expansis aliis desuper stantis : dexterâ, leonem: finistrã, bufonem fouendo contin gentis:dixit que aquila: Tua Marcomir progenies, caput meum subtitiet sibi: Leonem con culeabit simul occidet bufonem. Et ipse bufo subiecit: Non me, quod appareo foedus, rex pulcher aspernandum ducas. eft rebus specier mea conueniens forma futuris. Me primum extinguet generatio tua procul; post hac, leonem seruabit enfe captiuum: cuius ore quod amplius restat, audire curato. Leoninum postea caput Marcomiro regi dixit: Hospes in mea, fortiffime rex, cum gente tua venture, citó bufonem vinces labore, cum tempore multo, tunc mea suis cedent iura passim, vltro bellis astiu. Poslea me dextrum coronabit Aquila victum, habens à finistris tuo bufonem semine vinculum. Quod vero postea futurum erit, nostra tibi conuiuctio monstrat. His leoninum phantasma prolatis, tria in vnum subito capita sunt conuerfa, stabatque 20 monstrum triceps in hominis imaginem transformatum, nec simplicis à conditione, fed coronati aureo diademate regis, in finistrã sceptrum renentis, in dextera gladium, stridulaque voce submurmurans, sermone carminibus edoctâ suscitare manes, atque summos è calo deponere deos, responsètuis ferant praecantationibus, vt futuro futurum: intellige, ne frusta loquamur. Vt no stram confirmat imaginis transformatio formam, facit certam haec ipsa raticini vocem, sic genti futurum huic varium latum promittitur regnum, quod variabit tempus longum, generis multitudo regnantis, vt neque vnnum sit semper, neque permulta diuisum. Nunc vnum, tunc duo, nunc tria, tunc quatuor: vltra, nuncredit in vnum; postremo stabit in duo diuisum, cum Aquila fuerit amice coniuncta leoni, bufó finistram tenuerit insidians aquile partem. His omnibus dictis visio 30 dispartuit. Marcomirus rex, que esset vaticinij significatio, ab Aliruna requisitiut. Cui illa dixit: Deus est patritus, o rex, qui te comitatur gentem tuam, cuius informatius predictionibus, futura povo tuo regibus qui nascentur ex te: hinc quantocius tibi noueris esse migrandum ad vltimas terras leonis versus occidentem. Leo autem populum designat, qui ab ista parte Rheni fluminis habitat, antiqua Troianorum stirpe procreatus. Ab alia vero parte fluminis gens moratur bufonis, amplã fructiferam incolum regionem. Aliae gens tertia, que per equilam designtur, sunt Romani, quorum superbia vniversum mundum suo subiteere dominio laborat. Tu ergo vadecum populo tuo versus oc cidentem: habitabit is inter duas illes gentes, leonis bufonis, inter mare Rhenum. Futurus est enim, quod inter gentem tuam gentem bufonis gerentur praelia multa, plures ab vtraque parte 40 gladio cadent occisi. Postera die conuocatis iterum ad se proceribus, laudat confilium, fedes edicto publico monet omnino transferendas. Missa itaque legatione ad Saxones in Germaniam, qui ipsi ex Trojanis procreati memorantur, eos rogabant vt fratres, qua tenus in aliquo terrae suae angulo fedes manendi Scythis concederent. Quorum petitioni 50 Saxones facilem praebuere consensum, promittentes illis se daturos optimas fedes, nihiliominus adiicientes, vt venire quantocius festinarent. Vrgebat Saxones caussa, propter quam Scythis fratribus consensère libenter, vtpote quos inter se Gallos murum, pugnaculum ponere peroptabant. [unclear]. And each of you is by nature a brother to you and by nation a faithful friend. Go, with swift course take possession of the seats prepared, to be enlarged, by the will of the father, into a third part of the world.

That same night King Marcomirus summoned the ancestral deity by an incantation, with a murmured chant, and brought before him as prophetess one whom, because of her sagacity, they named Aliruna. He prepared a portent and confirmed the prophecy of the priestess by the authority of the Sibyl, and at once ordered the people to be led across, so that their offspring, multiplied exceedingly as the vision foretold, might remain stronger forever.

Marcomirus saw a three-headed deity standing there, and heard the separate prediction of each head; and he saw a distinct diadem placed high above each one. The first head was that of a toad; the second, of a lion; the third, in the form of an eagle, as if standing above with wings spread, holding and cherishing the lion on the right and the toad on the left. And the eagle said: “Marcomirus, your progeny shall subject my head to itself; it shall trample the lion and at the same time slay the toad.” And the toad itself added: “Do not think me to be despised, handsome king, because I appear foul. My outward form is suited to future events. Your generation will first destroy me far away; after this it will keep the lion captive by the sword. Take care to hear from his mouth what remains further.”

Afterward the lion’s head said to King Marcomirus: “Guest about to come into my [land], most valiant king, with your people, you will soon conquer the toad by toil; after much time, then my rights will everywhere yield to their own, of their own accord in wars [unclear]. Afterward the eagle on the right will crown me when conquered, having at the left the toad bound by your seed. What will happen afterward is shown to you by our conjunction.”

When the lion-shaped apparition had uttered these words, the three heads were suddenly changed into one, and the three-headed portent stood transformed into the image of a man, not of lowly condition, but of a king crowned with a golden diadem, holding a scepter in his left hand and a sword in his right. Muttering in a harsh voice, in speech taught by spells, to summon up the shades and to bring down the highest gods from heaven, it answered: “Let them bear with your enchantments, so that the future may be as future: understand, lest we speak in vain. As the transformation of our image confirms the form, so this very voice of prophecy makes certain that a kingdom, varied in condition, is promised in the future to this people; a long time will vary it, and the multitude of the ruling stock, so that it will neither always be one nor divided into very many. Now one, then two, now three, then four; beyond that, now it returns into one; at last it will stand divided into two, when the eagle has been joined as friend to the lion, and the toad, plotting against the eagle, has held the left side.” When all these things had been said, the vision disappeared.

King Marcomirus asked Aliruna what the meaning of the prophecy was. She said to him: “It is the ancestral god, O king, who accompanies you and your people; by his predictions you have been instructed about the future for your people and for the kings who will be born from you. From here you must know that you are to migrate as quickly as possible to the farthest lands of the lion toward the west. The lion designates the people who dwell on this side of the river Rhine, sprung from the ancient stock of the Trojans. On the other side of the river lives the people of the toad, inhabiting a broad and fruitful region. The third people, which is designated by the eagle, are the Romans, whose pride strives to subject the whole world to its dominion. Therefore go with your people toward the west. They will dwell between those two peoples, of the lion and of the toad, between the sea and the Rhine. For it will come to pass that many battles will be waged between your people and the people of the toad, and very many on both sides will fall slain by the sword.”

On the following day, when the nobles had again been summoned to him, he commended the plan and by public edict warned them that their settlements must altogether be transferred. And so an embassy was sent to the Saxons in Germany, who themselves are recorded as descended from the Trojans, and they asked them as brothers to allow the Scythians places to remain in some corner of their land. The Saxons readily gave consent to their petition, promising that they would give them excellent settlements, and nevertheless adding that they should hasten to come as quickly as possible. A cause pressed the Saxons on account of which they willingly agreed to the Scythians their brothers: namely, they very much desired to place them as a wall and bulwark between themselves and the Gauls.

On the arrival of the Scythians into the borders of Germany, to the parts [unclear], with their king Marcomirus: they were first Trojans, then Scythians, afterward Sicambri, and in the last generation were called Franks.

Therefore in the four hundred thirty-third year before the birth of Christ, which was the beginning of the seventh year of King Marcomirus, around the middle of the month Hecatombaeon, which the Romphaei, Saxons [unclear].

Saxons. [Bentius?] designates the Angles. Aliruna, that is, a wise-woman, [unclear]. A monstrous three-headed deity appeared. Words of the toad, that is [unclear], to the king. Galicia is designated as first to be overcome. Germany designates the lion to be conquered. Interpretation of the portent by Aliruna [unclear]. The varied change of the kingdom of the Franks. Aliruna [Gelbica?] is a wise-woman. By the lion, the Saxons; by the toad, the Gauls. The land of the Gallic toad, the German lion. Prophecy concerning the victory of the Franks. That the Franks would overcome the Romans. An embassy of the Franks is sent to the Saxons. The Saxons willingly admit the Trojan brothers. ANNAL. TRITHERMII. SECUNDVS. Antenor regis Marcomiri senior natu filius, codem anno sublimatus in regno, post patrem regnauit annis triginta, & maximo in honore apud suos est habitus, qui Saxonum amicitiam firmissimam sibi comparauit, quorum auxilio multa cum Romanis et Gallis praelia triumphantor commisit. Aduuabant eum Priamus et Nicanor frateres eius, cum reliquis ducibus continuatione fidelis, qui flumine transmisso, plures sape Gallis molestias intulerunt. Sunno quoque, patruus regis, cum filii suis ipsi Antenori summa cum fidelitate semper adhaesit in omnibus, ipsumque erudiuit in regimine proprium vt filium, venerabaturque nihilominus vt dominus. Vxorem habuit rex Antenor nomine Cambram, qua filia erat Belini regis Britannia. Hac fuit mulier super totius regni filias speciosissima, tantaque prudentia, vt eius consilio rex et principes Francorum, non fecus acnuminis cuiuisdam in cunctis semper consueuerit obtemperare. Mores gentis nimium Scythica feritate rudes adhuc, legibus reddidit cultiores, urbes et castella proceres adificare docuit. Iam ibi frontis cultum instituit, linum ferere, canapumque terra committere, atque in vestem venumque varium texere et aptare mulieribus scientiam dedit, leges compositit, ius dixit, vatem se Dianaque pontificem et Alirunanam exhibuit. Cumque mulierem sexu, regem vero ac sacerdotem gereret animo, Saxonibus a risu in proverbiun venit, vt quoties quaepiã praeter soluit prudentius aliqum gestient et aut loquentã audirent, quasi volente imitari prudentiam Cãbrae, increpantes dicebant: Ecce Camber. Quod corũ lingua sic dicitur: Si Camber, quasi dicerent. Num et tu Cambra calles prudentiam? Ita cum tẽpore inoleuit proverbiũ, quoe novissimae dictiones duae, hoc est, aduerbiũ et nomẽ Si et Camber, vni reddidere vocabulum, qu totum, facit Sicambrum. Mortuam vero post annos plures reginam, Sicambris retulerunt inter deas, & in memoriae eius regum procerumque decreto, qui prius Nouimagi, id est, Neumage, quasi novi cognati dicebantur Saxonibus amicis, deinceps vocabantur Sicambris, per annos ferme quadringentos, donec tandem a Franco rege quodam suo (quemadmodũ dicimus) nuncupati sunt Franci, vsque in praesentem diem, licet cum admixtione gentium. Interim vero quod fuerunt cum suis Troianis, etiam dicitur Troiani: cum Armenis, Armeni: cum Scythis, Scythae: cum Germanis, Germani: cum Gallis, Galli: & ab aliis frequenter aliud nomen consecuti, mores, linguam, idioma loquela, & vocabulum crebro cum sedibus mutauerunt. Anno Antenoris duodecimo, patruus eius Sunno moritur, duo relinquens filios, Marcomirum et Hecorem, quorum primus postea cum equo super glaciem cursitans, in Rheno fuit submersus: iunior vero, ducatum patris in Hollandia sub regis imperio gubernabat. Reliquit et alios quatuor filios, ex quatuor aliis concubinis procreatos, qui non computantur inter duces, lege Sicambrorum vetante, qua interdixit liberis de prima vxore superstitibus, filios sequentium principes vel esse vel nominari, quam legem Cambra tulit regina, ne regnum confunderetur. Priamus autem frater Antenoris regis, ducatum tenuit apud Grunes, in ea videlicet regione mari finitima, qua nunc dicitur Frisia, in qua oppidum Priami filius et dux, anno ante Christi nativitatem trecentesimo septuagesimo septimo condidit novum, quod ex suo nomine Gruningem nuncupatur vsque in praesentem diem. Erat enim duci nomen Grunus, a quo etiam populi (quamuis origine Franci) ad tempus dicti sunt Grunes. Antenor autem post multa fortiter gesta, moritur anno regni sui tricesimo: dominae vero nativitatis, cccc. lxxxii. quem Sicambris, more gentilitio, ingenti pompa prosequentes, iussu reginae in deos retulerunt. TERTIVS. Priamus regis Antenoris ex Cambra regina unicus filius, post patrem regnauit su per Sicambros, qui postea Franci sunt dicti, annis sex et viginti, cuius tempore Sicambrius populus sermonis patrii paulatim coepit obliuisci, & Saxonum vt lingua, in quorum confinibus morabantur. Remanerunt nihilominus ex vni vereri sermonis plura cum eis vocabula, quae Graecam resonare originem potius videntur, quam proprietatem linguae Theutonicae sive Germanorum, quod facile discernit, qui plenam lingua vtriusque habet notitiam. Nec subita fuit prisci sermonis in gente mutatio, quae tempore coepit, & vni tandem peruenit in naturam. Anno Priami regis sexto, mortuus est Marcomir dux, qui nepos fuit primi Sunnonis, de quo supra dictum est, quod cum aliis ducibus gentem perduxerit in Germaniam.
