In the first tome of Johannes Trithemius

Two volumes of Trithemius’s annals on the monastery of Hirsau, 59.3. Trithemius’s compendium or breviary, by whose work it was preserved, 63.2. [unclear], the opinion of which authors is followed, 42.54. Trudo, founder of the monastery of [Harbas?], 56.4. The borders of the Tungri, seats of the kings of the Franks, 27.95. Turpin, archbishop of Reims: what he wrote, and when, 255.20. Tiberius Caesar the Roman, defeated by the Franks, 15.40. The tyranny of King Clovis toward his kinsmen, 41.14. The county of Tyrol is subjected to Rudolph, duke of Austria, 134.24.

Valentinian Caesar, who reigned with Theodosius, attempts to destroy the Franks, 31.18; they are forced to retreat into Italy, ibid. 24; he makes the Franks tributaries, ibid. 27. Valentinian demands tribute from the Franks, 31.53. Valentinian the emperor dies by a noose, 32.51. Valentinian, Roman emperor, wages war with the Saxons [unclear], not far from the [unclear], 28.29. The Vascones are defeated by the Franks, 72.10. The prophecy of Hildegast concerning the arms and power of the king of the Franks, 21.30. Vadricius, monk of Strasbourg: what he wrote, and when, 141.50. [Vecheslinius?], from whom he received his name, 19.12. Vecchanus, high priest, prophet, and historiographer of the Franks, 19.4. Vecthania, priest of the Franks, perishes in water, 19.11. The priests of Venus, virgins, admit young men at certain times of the year, 66.27; afterward they are first forced to leave the temple of [unclear], ibid. 32. Truth proved by duel, 24.42. Vernus, bishop of Hispalis: what he wrote, and when, 249.21. Victor of Maximilian dies by the sword, 31.9. Victorius the African: what he wrote, and when, 205.36. Victorinus of Marseille, rhetor: what he wrote, and when, 228.6. Victorinus, bishop of [Pitriauium?]: what he wrote, 199.51. Victorinus Aquitanicus: what he wrote, and when, 232.30. Victorinus Buconius, bishop: what he wrote, and when, 233.16. Vigilius, deacon and monk: what he wrote, and when, 225.6. Vincentius, priest: what he wrote, and when, 233.31. Vincentius Gruner of Zwickau, doctor of Prague: what he wrote, and when, 152.15. When wine began among the Mosellans, 84.23. Seventy-one thousand virgins from Britain, to be sent to Armorica, are gathered at London, 30.10. The virgins are endangered at sea, 30.16; a great part are drowned, ibid. 20; captured by barbarians, they are killed, 22.63. The history of the virgins perishing at sea, 77.48. [Utellius?] the African: what he wrote, and when, 17.7. Vitas on the Moselle, handed over by the Franks from eastern Francia, 84.16. Queen Ulida, pregnant, is killed in a hunt together with her husband, 91.42. Vsinius, monk: what he wrote, and when, 23.17. Who the father of Saint Ursula was, 77.53. Ursula, a very beautiful virgin and very devoted to Christ, 29.16; she is sought by Conan as wife, 30.1. [Uther Pendragon?], son of the king of Britain, 39.14. Vulpiseu Welf legally acquires the duchy of Bavaria, dedicated to the rightful heir, 107.4.

Walamirus, king of the Ostrogoths, together with the Huns devastates the empire, 37.4. Walricus, monk, 54.15. Walfridus, abbot of the monastery of St. Gall: what he wrote, and when he flourished, 12.4, 14.19, 17. Walther, king of the Franks, 33; how many years he reigned, 23.16; when he died, ibid. 6. From what origin the Vandals had their beginning, 83.5. Twenty thousand Vandals are slaughtered by the Franks, 83.5. The Vandals cross the Rhine, 33.4. Twenty thousand Vandals, together with their king Godgibst, are killed by the Franks, 34.11. The Vandals make Gobigsith king for themselves in Gaul, 33.11. The Vandals, leaving Gaul, occupy part of the Spains and dwell there for nearly thirty years, 34.5; they destroy Hippo [unclear], ibid. 6. The Vandals enter Francia and are put to flight, 93.10. Wanninus, monk and hermit, 14.9. Wandelbertius, deacon and monk of Prum: what he wrote, and when he flourished, 127.27, 25.20. Who Wandregisilus was, and when he flourished, 17.8. Wanius and Melga, kings of the Huns and Picts, devastate Britain, 30.46; they are driven into Ireland, ibid. 52. Wanni, king of the Huns, and Melga, king of the Picts, hired for pay by Gratian, afflict the borders of Germany and Gaul, 30.27. Three hundred eighty-five thousand Vascones are slaughtered in one day, 93.5. How far Wasthaldus carried the Frankish history, 4.13. Welf, duke of Bavaria, unjustly dismisses Ethelina his wife, 107.16; removed from the duchy, he is restored, ibid. 34; he sets out for the Holy Land, ibid. 36. Welf, duke of Bavaria, sends his son into Italy, 108.5. Wesel, the village where the Lippe flows into the Rhine, 97.18. The region of the Westphalians received into surrender by Charlemagne, 28.2; called Saxons, 46.38. Wilbertius, bishop of Chartres: what he wrote, and when, 243.12. William of Oppenbach, doctor of Paris: what he wrote, 149.3.

William of Oppenbach, doctor of Paris, 149.3.
